why_tracked: Owns the workhorse and accessible segment, is moving upmarket into industrial SLS, and is advertising directly into drone manufacturing.
headline: Formlabs is now selling large-format industrial SLS into drone manufacturing, and it ships the Fuse X1 before HP ships the MJF 1200.
so_what: The accessible-industrial segment we assumed HP would define in 2027 is being defined by Formlabs in Q4 2026. Formlabs is naming drone customers by name in outbound and its resellers are running drone-specific campaigns with quote CTAs. This is our Drone Dominance ground, contested from below rather than from above.

linkedin.note: Advertiser search 'Formlabs'. Reported total 38 ads, hand-counted to 38 across 15 unique creatives. Reconciled.

items.t: Formlabs tested a drone-team conversation ad signed by a named rep. It ran two weeks and reached under 1,000 people.
items.d: Rob Ortiz, personalised with %FIRSTNAME%, claims Skyfall, the largest drone manufacturer in Ukraine, prints flight-ready parts the same day they are designed, and quotes the Fuse X1 at 20 one-foot quadcopter frames per build versus 7-10 days and 5x the cost at a service bureau. Because it was served in the EU, LinkedIn discloses the full record: Aug 10-24 2026, under 1,000 total impressions, 97% United States, targeted only on language and broad location. Read it as a message test, not a campaign. The claim is the finding; the reach is not.

items.t: Three instances of the 'From prototype to propeller-ready' SLS drone creative are in rotation.
items.d: Mixed video and single image, top-funnel, all pointing at end-use drone components with 'no supports, no compromise'. The operative words are 'end-use' and 'production-grade'.

items.t: The paid mix is overwhelmingly top-funnel prototyping, not production.
items.d: 26 of 38 instances (68%) are top-funnel. The single largest creative, 'Turn concepts into reality faster', runs 8 instances on its own, 21% of total ad volume, and has been live since at least April 2026. Formlabs buys reach on prototyping and reserves production claims for outbound and executive thought-leader posts.

items.t: Fuse X1 launched June 9 2026 at $84,999, shipping Q4 2026.
items.d: 330 x 330 x 565 mm build volume, Nylon 12 plus Open Material Mode at launch, Nylon 11 end of 2026, Nylon 12 GF and TPU announced. Claims up to 50% lower cost per part and 3x throughput versus comparable industrial powder bed fusion, install in about an hour through a standard industrial door.

items.t: Formlabs is in early talks over a roughly $500M IPO.
items.d: Reported Aug 7 2026. SoftBank-backed. An IPO track usually means a marketing spend increase and louder production-scale claims, not a quieter competitor. [Unverified] as to whether it proceeds.

items.t: Former Apple hardware chief Dan Riccio took a stake and became strategic adviser, Aug 12 2026.
items.d: Advising on product development, design rigor and operational scaling. Paired with a wider management reshuffle that trade press reads as pointing toward an exit event.

items.t: Formlabs says three more printer platforms ship within 12 months, after a record Q3.
items.d: Technologies and price points unspecified. Assume continued downward price pressure in the accessible-industrial band through 2027.

items.t: The core claim is price-performance parity, stated explicitly by the CRO.
items.d: Nick Graham, CRO, runs thought-leader ads asking 'Can a $7,000 3D printer outperform one that costs $100,000/year?' and answering yes, citing #1 unit market share in industrial resin printers. The argument is that scale economics remove the tradeoff, so there is 'no waiting game of months or years trying to reach breakeven ROI'.

items.t: Formlabs is attacking the 'resin is not for production' objection head on.
items.d: The Clove Dental creative opens with 'Resin 3D printing isn't ready for production. It's a common misconception'. Reliability is quantified: 98.6% print success on Form 4B, 98.3% on Form 4BL, from 400,000+ customer votes, plus a commissioned third-party study at 98.7% part yield.

items.t: Dental is a separately-messaged funnel run by an executive, not by brand.
items.d: 3 of 4 thought-leader instances are dental. Formlabs treats dental as its proven production vertical and then uses it as evidence when selling engineering and manufacturing.

items.t: Resellers, not Formlabs, are running the hardest drone creative.
items.d: Phillips Machine Tools runs at least four distinct drone campaigns on Formlabs SLS, including 'Lightweight drone parts. Printed in-house. Ready in 24 hours', 'Are production delays slowing your next launch?', 'Build Your Drone Manufacturing Facility', and a Fuse FX prototype-to-production ad. CTAs are 'Get a Quote today' and 'Talk to our team'. Bottom-funnel, aimed at exactly the buyer we are calling.

items.t: Thinglab and 3D-EDU GmbH are running Fuse X1 launch webinars in APAC and DACH.
items.d: Thinglab ran a 'first look at the brand new Fuse X1' event on Aug 5 2026 across multiple instances. 3D-EDU is running the German-language equivalent. Formlabs uses the channel to carry launch education while corporate holds top-funnel brand spend.

talk_track.claim: "The Fuse X1 gives you industrial large-format SLS for under $85,000, and it ships this quarter."
talk_track.counter: Price of entry is not cost of ownership. Ask what the qualified material set is on day one: Nylon 12 and Open Material Mode, with Nylon 11 not until end of 2026 and GF and TPU still to come. Then ask what happens when the part needs a flame-retardant, ESD-safe or high-temperature material for an airframe. Open Material Mode moves the qualification burden onto the customer.

talk_track.claim: "Skyfall, the largest drone manufacturer in Ukraine, prints flight-ready parts the same day they are designed on our machines."
talk_track.counter: Do not dispute it, reframe it. Same-day iteration is a prototyping win and we do it too. Ask what the qualification and traceability package looks like once the part becomes a flight-critical production article on a defense program. Note this claim appears only in outbound copy: Formlabs has a published ORQA case study but no published Skyfall case study. Treat it as [Unverified].

talk_track.claim: "A $7,000 printer outperforms one that costs $100,000 a year. There are no tradeoffs."
talk_track.counter: That comparison is against a service bureau contract, not against an owned production system. It is a true statement about prototyping economics and a misleading one about production. Move to parts per year, material qualification, repeatability across machines, and what happens at the second and third site.

talk_track.claim: "Resin and SLS are production technologies now. Look at 98.6% print success and dental at volume."
talk_track.counter: Print success rate is a machine reliability metric, not a part qualification metric. Dental aligner moulds are a forgiving, single-material, single-geometry application. Ask them to show the same numbers on a load-bearing airframe component against a documented material spec.

talk_track.claim: Reseller pitch: "Lightweight drone parts. Printed in-house. Ready in 24 hours."
talk_track.counter: 24 hours to a part is not 24 hours to a qualified part. This is a channel message with a 'Get a Quote' CTA, which means the reseller is quoting fast and cheap. Expect it where the buyer is an engineering manager with a departmental budget rather than a program office.

exposure: Drone manufacturing as a named vertical. Formlabs has a dedicated drones industry page, a published ORQA case study, top-funnel SLS drone creative and a personalised outbound drone play. This is not adjacent to Drone Dominance, it is the same buyer.

In-house production versus service bureau. The Fuse X1 outbound explicitly frames the decision as bringing production in-house instead of outsourcing. That is our argument, made at a fifth of the price.

Accessible industrial SLS timing. Fuse X1 ships Q4 2026. HP's MJF 1200 does not ship until early 2027. Formlabs gets a full runway in the segment before HP arrives, and we should stop assuming HP is the competitor that defines it.
The reseller channel. Phillips Machine Tools is running bottom-funnel, quote-seeking drone campaigns. Channel-led competition reaches accounts our direct team may never see in a CRM.

watch.b: Watch for slip. A delay past Q4 opens the same gap we are already exploiting against HP's MJF 1200.
A $500M raise would fund a marketing step-change. Track an S-1 filing, which would also disclose real revenue and R&D numbers for the first time.
Unnamed technologies and price points. If one is a higher-temperature or engineering-polymer platform it moves directly into our territory.

watch.h: Whether the Skyfall claim gets a published case study
watch.b: Right now it exists only in outbound copy. If Formlabs publishes it, expect it in every drone deal we are in.
Reseller drone campaigns are the leading indicator of where Formlabs is finding traction. Re-count next run and set a trend.

unverified: Skyfall, the largest drone manufacturer in Ukraine, uses Formlabs printers. [Unverified] Claimed in a Formlabs conversation ad. Skyfall is independently confirmed as Ukraine's primary interceptor drone manufacturer and its P1-Sun is a 3D printed modular interceptor, but no published Formlabs case study or Skyfall statement names Formlabs. Do not repeat it as fact and do not assert it is false.
Fuse X1 delivers up to 50% lower cost per part and 3x throughput versus comparable industrial powder bed fusion. [Unverified] Vendor claim, no named comparison system or test method disclosed.

Clove Dental manufactures 50,000 clear aligners a day. [Unverified] The ad body says 'a day' and then says 'more than half a million parts a year', inconsistent by roughly a factor of 30. The card headline elsewhere reads 'per month'. Treat the figure as unreliable as published.

98.6% Form 4B print success rate from 400,000+ customer votes. [Unverified] Self-reported telemetry on a self-selected voting mechanic. The commissioned third-party 98.7% part yield study is cited but not published in the ad.
Formlabs is '#1 by unit market share' in industrial resin 3D printers. [Unverified] No source cited in the ad.

Earlier in this run the Skyfall conversation ad was described as the highest-priority creative. That overstated it. It is strategically revealing but operationally tiny: under 1,000 impressions over two weeks, now ended. Corrected on the same day.
